course_name_original: Modelos y Métodos de Organización Industrial
course_name_en: Models and Methods of Industrial Organization
prerequisites: Knowledge of Linear Programming (from 'Planificación y Control de la Producción')
Recommended: English language skills to read and understand scientific articles and manuals

learning_outcomes.text: Possess and understand knowledge that provides a basis or opportunity to be original in the development and/or application of ideas, often in a research context.
Students know how to apply the acquired knowledge and their problem-solving capacity in new or little-known environments within broader (or multidisciplinary) contexts related to their area of study.
Students possess the learning skills that will allow them to continue studying in a largely self-directed or autonomous way.

Have adequate knowledge of the scientific and technological aspects of: mathematical, analytical and numerical methods in engineering, electrical engineering, energy engineering, chemical engineering, mechanical engineering, continuum mechanics, industrial electronics, automation, manufacturing, materials, quantitative management methods, industrial informatics, urbanism and infrastructures.
Carry out strategic planning and apply it to constructive and production, quality and environmental management systems.
Technically and economically manage projects, facilities, plants, companies and technology centers.
Be able to exercise general management, technical management and R&D&i project management functions in plants, companies and technology centers.
Ability to design and project automated production systems and advanced process control.
Knowledge and abilities to organize and manage companies.
Knowledge and abilities of strategy and planning applied to different organizational structures.
Knowledge of management information systems, industrial organization, productive and logistics systems, and quality management systems.
Model and solve real mathematical optimization problems in the context of industrial organization.
Model and solve network optimization problems.
Model and solve problems using metaheuristics.

syllabus_topics: Continuous and integer linear optimization: Network optimization models

assessment_methods.method: Individual work (TI): Report on proposing and solving a problem using metaheuristics
Team work (TG): Presentation of a scientific article with a practical application of methods studied
Class participation (PC) and lab practice reports

assessment_rules: The final grade is calculated as TI + TG + PC + EX, where TI is worth a maximum of 3 points, TG 2 points, PC 1 point, and EX 4 points. A minimum score of 1.5 points is required on the exam to pass the course. For class participation, attendance at 80% of laboratory practices is mandatory. In extraordinary calls, TI, TG, and PC scores from the ordinary call are preserved, and a new practical exam (EX) is taken.
